socfpga_reboot_mngr.h

Reboot Manager hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
REBOOT_WARM

Identifier to initiate a Warm Reboot. A warm reboot asserts the HPS warm reset request, allowing the Secure Device Manager (SDM) to gracefully reset the CPU subsystem while preserving certain FPGA and system states.

REBOOT_COLD

Identifier to initiate a Cold Reboot. A cold reboot triggers a hard reset of the entire system, equivalent to a physical power cycle. All volatile states across the HPS, SDM, and FPGA will be lost.

Types
reboot_callback_t

Callback function signature used by the Reboot Manager module. This allows the application to register a shutdown hook that will be executed immediately before the hardware reset is triggered. It is critical for flushing caches, unmounting filesystems, or parking external peripherals safely.

Parameters
param

An opaque pointer to user context that will be passed directly to the callback function when invoked.

reboot_mngr_set_callback
int32_t reboot_mngr_set_callback(
reboot_callback_t 
callback,
uint32_t 
event
)

Registers a user-defined function to be executed as a pre-reset hook. The application should use this to ensure software state is saved or hardware is safely halted before the physical reboot line is asserted.

Parameters
callback
reboot_callback_t

The function pointer to invoke before the reboot occurs.

event
uint32_t

The target reset type for this callback (REBOOT_WARM or REBOOT_COLD).

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the event identifier is unrecognized.

reboot_mngr_do_reboot
int32_t reboot_mngr_do_reboot(
uint32_t 
event
)

Initiates the physical reboot sequence. This function first checks for and executes any registered reboot_callback_t for the specified event type.  Once the callback completes, it writes to the hardware Reset Manager or SDM Mailbox to assert the physical reset line.

Parameters
event
uint32_t

The desired reset sequence to trigger (REBOOT_WARM or REBOOT_COLD).

Returns

If successful, this function will never return as the system will reset.  It returns -EINVAL if the argument is invalid, or -ENOTSUP if the specific reboot type is not supported by the underlying hardware configuration.
